newsitem.title: USA: U.S FDA issues warning on Royal Line smoked salmon.
newsitem.headline: U.S FDA issues warning on Royal Line smoked salmon.

text.p: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration on Tuesday warned consumers not to eat Royal Line smoked salmon because the product may be contaminated with bacteria.

Florida-based Marine Marketing International Inc, which had imported the salmon from Denmark, initiated its own recall and ceased shipments of the product from the processor, the agency said in a statement.

The recall affects about 3,000 packages of sliced, skinless and boneless salmon, packed in 2.5 lb heat-sealed vacuum plastic bags and labeled Royal Line bank smoked salmon, Faroe Islands. Packaging does not carry a product code.

Routine testing by FDA turned up Listeria monocytogenes, an organism that can cause serious and sometimes fatal infection in small children, frail or elderly people, and people with weakened immune systems.
No illnesses have been reported to date, FDA said.

The scope of distribution is uncertain because the sole distributor of the product, Marcos Marketing Innovations Co of Marietta, Georgia, has refused to cooperate in providing information or recalling the salmon, FDA said.

However, the company said all the packages were distributed in one week to synagogues and clubs for use in fund-raising events. It said they were already consumed and there was nothing left to recall. The packages were not distributed to retail markets.
Responding to charges of being uncooperative, Marcos Vincent, a spokesman for the company, told Reuters: "If I thought it (the salmon) was dangerous, I would have cooperated.
"If they (FDA) had done their job of checking the product prior to it clearing customs, then it could have been sent back to the processor," Vincent said.
Vincent said the FDA never checked for the listeria until after it had been cleared customs and distributed for consumption.
The salmon is processed and smoked in Denmark, FDA said.
